name_reason: Fully compliant: data_fd2_ prefix (game global data), chapter domain, ch27 is a meaningful chapter ID (range 01-30, kept), end_scene_char_pos_x_table accurately describes the data (end-scene per-char X tile positions) and reflects the data type via the _table suffix. No Ghidra address residue (no hex suffix equal to its own/any address). Live Ghidra symbol matches byte-identically.
purpose: Chapter 27 end-scene X tile positions for runtime char slots 0..15, read by fd2_chapter_27_end to place the party before the GOOD/BAD ending fork.
logic_summary: const uint8[16] private read-only table. fd2_chapter_27_end @ 0x250CC copies it onto stack scratch via MOVSD x4 (16 bytes), then passes the stack pointer to fd2_setup_chars_and_camera_for_intro, which indexes it by char slot (paired with the Y table @ 0x52316). Not consumed by any other function.
element_semantics: Each element [i] is the world X tile coordinate at which runtime char slot i (0..15) is placed for the chapter-27 end scene; values 0x0C..0x12 are map tile columns.
notes: Two xrefs to 0x52306 (0x250e3 DATA = MOV ESI address-load; 0x250e8 READ = MOVSD load), both inside fd2_chapter_27_end and both reads -> zero game-side writer confirms const (C already declares const uint8). Memory @ 0x52306 = 0F 0F 0C 0D 11 12 0D 0E 10 11 0E 0F 10 0E 0F 10, matches the C definition exactly. Ghidra data plate was null; created a concise plate (PLATE_COMMENT) reflecting the src conclusion. src comment block (lines 664-674) is accurate/precise/ASCII so kept as-is; no src edit. Save of Ghidra .gpr left to the user per project rule (not backing up).
